question: Which owner should reconcile browser input, IME, DOM mutations and document changes without competing write paths?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest stop verdict, at queue position 7 in the plite-view group. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Each accepted user edit publishes through a canonical document transaction, with explicit arbitration between model-owned commands and accepted native text.
IME composition, Android pending diffs and composition history grouping keep their mounted-view lifetimes; one composition joins one history group.
Unauthorized DOM mutations never become document truth; the integrity observer restores them outside composition and Android ownership.
Ordinary applications declare no input-safety or fast-path flags; renderer capability is published by the renderer owner (docs/vision/plite.md fast-path law).
Browser editing claims need model, DOM, selection, focus and follow-up typing proof (VISION.md), so any replacement must hold native parity in every supported engine.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-12 lanes and the 5066 safety-flag and long-IME history decisions as context, without transferring their historical test claims. Rechecked on the live tree the controller construction in editable-dom-runtime.ts, Android and root-claim arbitration in runtime-input-events.ts, the native-text writer in input-history.ts and its callers in dom-repair-queue.ts and composition-state.ts, the model command path in mutation-controller.ts, integrity restoration in dom-integrity-observer.ts, keydown handling in keyboard-input-strategy.ts, EditableProps (no input-safety flags), and the autocomplete plans' native decisions (settleInput, the refused Plite-wide IME-confirm filter).
summary: The job is to turn browser input (beforeinput, native text, IME composition, Android pending diffs, keydown) into canonical document changes without double insertion, lost input or split undo, and to keep the DOM from drifting into a second truth. Live source still has the reviewed shape. EditableDOMRuntime builds its input controller over the root's shared DOMInputRuntime. Model-owned intents go through applyEditableCommand and the command chain, accepted native text goes through updateNativeTextInput with one native-grouping annotation, Android owns repair while its manager is mounted, a root-claimed input suppresses the React repair, and the integrity observer reverts unowned, non-canonical mutations outside composition and Android ownership. The autocomplete work since 2026-09-12 added api.react.settleInput and composition reads under this owner, and its panel refused a Plite-wide IME-confirm key filter because TablePlugin needs keyCode 229 at composition start. The strongest remaining cut, folding router, controller, kernel and event engines into one runtime, would shrink the 85 tracked files and about 35,000 lines of layering under react/editable but moves no ownership, so it is Refactoring work, not an architecture verdict.

alternatives: Keeping the per-Editable controller over the shared DOMInputRuntime, with two canonical write paths and integrity restore, wins. Each input family has one arbiter, and both paths end in canonical transactions.

Deleting or merging the router, controller, kernel and event-engine layers into one runtime loses as an architecture change. It removes forwarding and file count but no owner, state or write path, and the size (85 tracked files, about 35,000 lines under react/editable, counted with wc) belongs to a Refactoring audit.
Making every input model-owned (preventDefault on all beforeinput) loses. IME composition and Android keyboards mutate the DOM before any cancelable event, so reconciliation is still required.

Replace contenteditable reconciliation with the EditContext API: loses for now. It is not available in every supported engine, so it could only be an extra strategy and would not remove the current one.

Adding a Plite-wide filter that withholds IME-confirm keydowns (isComposing or keyCode 229) from every Editable onKeyDown loses. The autocomplete panel refused it because TablePlugin collapses a cell selection on the keyCode 229 keydown that starts a composition, and Plite already withholds keys while its own composition flag is set.

Moving typed-text classification into the native owner, so Plate stops reading private input tags, is the right direction, but it belongs to the autocomplete Pursue's Phase 1b (another session's uncommitted typed-text work), so it is excluded here.
proofLimits: Source review only; no test, browser, IME or device run. Double insertion, lost pending input, split undo and repair during composition stay regression risks this review does not re-prove. WebKit's IME-confirm Enter on a real IME and Android Gboard behavior are unproven here. Another session has uncommitted typed-text edits in composition-state.ts, dom-repair-queue.ts, model-input-strategy.ts, mutation-controller.ts, android-input-manager.ts, diff-text.ts and with-react.ts that wrap these writers with withTypedTextIntent; they add a report and do not change the write path, but they shift the cited lines in those files (HEAD line numbers are given where it matters). The decisive IME-confirm refusal rests on the autocomplete session's staged, uncommitted plan, and the Plate shortcut-table skip it relies on is also uncommitted. EditContext engine support comes from general knowledge, not a check run here.
